candidateOutcomes.text: Select and analyze a suitable topic by collecting and organizing relevant data for a seminar.
Prepare and deliver an effective seminar presentation using appropriate communication and presentation tools.
Demonstrate critical thinking and engagement by encouraging discussion, interaction, and knowledge sharing during the seminar.

Identify a real-world problem and formulate a project plan including objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes for capstone implementation. IV. General Guidelines for Seminar and Project Initiation  The seminar must be related to emerging trends in the engineering/technology programme or may be inter/multi-disciplinary, based on industry expectations and programme outcomes.  Individual students have different aptitudes and strengths. Therefore, the seminar should match the strengths of the students. For this purpose, students shall be asked to select the title(theme) of the seminar they would like to prepare and present.  Seminar titles are to be finalized in consultation with the faculty mentor.  The seminar must involve logical development and application of various technologies/processes applicable in the industry.  The seminar must be assigned to an individual student. However, support from other students may be taken during presentation, if required.  Students are required to prepare their seminar using relevant software tools and written content for presentation.  Students shall submit one hard copy and one soft copy of the presentation and may be encouraged to keep a recorded copy of the seminar presentation.  A batch of 3-4 students shall be formed for project initiation.  Projects provide a platform for students to demonstrate an attitude of inquiry and identify problem statements related to their programme.  Students shall identify information suggesting the cause of the problem and possible solutions.  Students shall study and assess the feasibility of different solutions along with financial implications.  Students should collect relevant data from various sources such as books, the internet, market, suppliers, and experts (through surveys/interviews).  Students shall prepare the required drawings/designs and a detailed plan for successful execution of the project.  Students may visit relevant organizations related to the problem statement as part of the initial study. V. Guidelines for Seminar Preparation and Presentation Once the seminar title/topic is finalized and allotted, the teacher’s role becomes important as a guide, mentor, and motivator to promote learning and sustain student interest. The following should be kept in mind while preparing and presenting the seminar:  Seminar Orientation and Briefing: Topics/themes should be innovative, novel, and relevant to the programme curriculum, and aligned with industry expectations.  Seminar Literature Survey (Information Search and Data Collection): The information and data collected should be authentic, realistic, and relevant to the curriculum.
